description: A sixteen-panel composite (three different panel kinds) of Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C (x = 4, 6, 8, 10 wt.%) low-density steels; the EBSD phase maps carry the headline claim and the TEM panels supply the ordering evidence. (a-d) EBSD phase maps (red = austenite γ, blue = ferrite α): (a) 4Al is almost entirely red with thin white lines, scale bar 100 μm; (b) 6Al is red-dominant with sparse blue grains (100 μm); (c) 8Al is blue-dominant with many red γ grains, its printed scale bar reads 100 nm; (d) 10Al is nearly all blue (200 μm). (e-h) are [100]γ SADPs with red-circled 022γ/020γ reflections and, for 6Al-10Al, a yellow-circled 011_SRO spot absent in (e). (i, k, m) are [110]α // [110]_DO3 ferrite SADPs labelling red 11̄0α, 11̄2α, 002α and yellow 1̄11_DO3, 002_DO3, 001_B2 superlattice spots. (j, l, n) are paired dark-field images from the 1̄11_DO3 and 002_DO3 reflections (50 nm bars) with green/yellow arrows marking intensity differences. (o) is TEM of acicular 18R martensite (1 μm) and (p) four EDS maps (Mn, C, Fe, Al; 200 nm). The panels together show that increasing Al drives γ → ferrite-based duplex and promotes B2/DO3 ordering plus 18R martensite. No numeric phase fractions are printed.
measured_quantities: austenite/ferrite phase constitution from EBSD phase maps (relative area, no numeric values printed)
size of DO3 ordered domains (nm), reported only in the citing text
scale bars in μm (EBSD, TEM morphology) and nm (dark-field TEM, EDS maps)

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows the 4Al steel as an almost fully red (austenite) EBSD phase map traversed by thin white lines within the grains, with a 100 μm scale bar.
Panel (c) labels both γ (red) and α (blue) in the 8Al steel, with blue ferrite forming the matrix and red austenite the minority grains, whereas panel (b) for 6Al has red austenite as the matrix.
Panel (d) shows the 10Al steel phase map as almost entirely blue ferrite with only isolated small red austenite regions, using a 200 μm scale bar.
The scale bar printed inside panel (c) reads '100 nm', which is inconsistent with the 100 μm and 200 μm bars in the other EBSD phase maps of the same row.

Panel (e) for 4Al austenite shows only red-circled γ reflections labelled 022γ and 020γ, with no yellow-circled SRO spot, while panels (f-h) for 6Al, 8Al and 10Al each add a yellow-circled SRO reflection (011_SRO / 0-11_SRO) and the annotation [100]γ // [100]_SRO.
Panels (i), (k) and (m) are ferrite SADPs indexed along [110]α // [110]_DO3, with red circles on 11̄0α, 11̄2α and 002α and yellow circles on the superlattice reflections 1̄11_DO3, 002_DO3 and 001_B2.

Panels (j), (l) and (n) each consist of two stacked dark-field TEM images (50 nm scale bars) taken from the 1̄11_DO3 and 002_DO3 reflections in the same field of view, with green and yellow arrows marking regions of lower and higher relative intensity.

Panel (o) is a TEM image of the 10Al steel showing needle-shaped features annotated '18R' (1 μm scale bar), and panel (p) presents Mn, C, Fe and Al EDS maps of the same feature with 200 nm scale bars.
The caption states that the austenite SADPs (e-h) are along the [001] zone axis, whereas the patterns themselves are labelled [100]γ; the image and caption readings disagree on the zone-axis index.

The caption states that (a-d) are EBSD phase maps in which red represents austenite and blue represents ferrite, and that (j, l, n) are TEM dark-field images acquired using the (111) and (002) DO3 superlattice reflections.

The citing text states that 4Al is single-phase FCC γ austenite, 6Al an austenite-based duplex steel, and 8Al and 10Al ferrite-based duplex steels, with quasi-equiaxed grains and annealing twin boundaries shown as white lines.

The citing text attributes the satellite spots near the γ reflections to Al and C concentration fluctuations indicating spinodal decomposition during quenching, and the very weak {110} spots in 6Al, 8Al and 10Al to an L12-type short-range ordered structure whose intensity decreases with increasing Al content.

The citing text reports maximum DO3 ordered-domain sizes of approximately 2.0 nm (6Al), 2.1 nm (8Al) and 19 nm (10Al), increasing with nominal Al content; these numbers are not printed anywhere on the figure.

The citing text states that the acicular precipitates in the ferrite of the 10Al steel are 18R martensite enriched in Mn and C and depleted in Al, consistent with the dashed-arrow annotations in panel (p).

subfigures.description: EBSD phase map of the 4Al steel: the whole field is red (austenite γ, labelled) with thin white lines cutting the grains (identified as annealing twin boundaries in the citing text); essentially no blue ferrite; scale bar 100 μm.
EBSD phase map of the 6Al steel: red austenite matrix (γ labelled) with a minority of blue ferrite (α labelled), mostly at grain boundaries; scale bar 100 μm.
EBSD phase map of the 8Al steel: blue ferrite matrix (α labelled) with numerous red austenite grains (γ labelled); the printed scale bar reads 100 nm, which is anomalous for an EBSD map.
EBSD phase map of the 10Al steel: field almost entirely blue ferrite (α labelled) with only a few isolated small red austenite regions (γ labelled); scale bar 200 μm.
SAED pattern of 4Al austenite labelled [100]γ; red circles mark the 022γ and 020γ reflections; no SRO/superlattice spot is circled in this panel.
[100]γ SADP of 6Al austenite with red-circled 022γ and 020γ reflections plus a yellow-circled 011_SRO reflection; yellow annotation [100]γ // [100]_SRO.
[100]γ SADP of 8Al austenite with red-circled 022γ, 020γ and yellow-circled 011_SRO reflections; the SRO index label is only partially legible.
[100]γ SADP of 10Al austenite with red-circled 022γ, 020γ and a yellow-circled reflection labelled 0-11_SRO.
SAED pattern of 6Al ferrite along [110]α // [110]_DO3 with red-circled α reflections 11̄0α, 11̄2α, 002α and yellow-circled 1̄11_DO3, 002_DO3, 001_B2 superlattice reflections.

Two stacked dark-field TEM images of 6Al ferrite acquired from the 1̄11_DO3 (top) and 002_DO3 (bottom) reflections in the same field of view; green and yellow arrows mark regions of different brightness; 50 nm scale bars.
SAED pattern of 8Al ferrite along [110]α // [110]_DO3 with the same red-circled α spots and yellow-circled 1̄11_DO3, 002_DO3, 001_B2 superlattice spots.
Two stacked dark-field TEM images of 8Al ferrite from the 1̄11_DO3 (top) and 002_DO3 (bottom) reflections, with green and yellow arrows; 50 nm scale bars.

SAED pattern of 10Al ferrite along [110]α // [110]_DO3 with red-circled 11̄0α, 11̄2α, 002α and yellow-circled 1̄11_DO3, 002_DO3, 001_B2 reflections; the superlattice spots appear the most intense of the three ferrite patterns.
Two stacked dark-field TEM images of 10Al ferrite from the 1̄11_DO3 (top) and 002_DO3 (bottom) reflections, with green and yellow arrows; 50 nm scale bars.
TEM microstructure of the 10Al steel showing acicular/needle-shaped features inside a ferrite grain; dashed white arrows labelled '18R' point along the needles; scale bar 1 μm.

Four EDS elemental maps labelled Mn, C, Fe and Al (200 nm scale bars each) of the same acicular feature; dashed white arrows point at the needle in every map. Contrast is low, so enrichment is read from the arrows and the citing text rather than from intensity values.

unreadable_items: panel (c): the printed scale bar reads '100 nm', which contradicts the μm-scale of the other EBSD maps in the same row; the intended unit cannot be confirmed from the pixels
panel (g): the SRO spot index is only partially legible (011_SRO vs 0-11_SRO)
panels (i), (k), (m): the superscript/subscript Miller indices of the yellow-circled B2/DO3 spots are small and only partly legible at the supplied resolution
panel (o): the fine internal structure/width of the 18R needles is not resolvable, and no thickness or length values are printed
panel (p): individual EDS maps are low-contrast; relative Mn/C enrichment is inferred from the arrows and citing text, not from printed intensity values
no numeric phase fractions, grain sizes or domain sizes are printed on any EBSD or SADP panel
